claims.text: High configurational entropy thermodynamically favors a single-phase solid solution in bulk high-entropy alloys.
The high surface-to-volume ratio of high-entropy alloy nanoparticles lowers the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Enhanced surface diffusion in nanoparticles negates the sluggish-diffusion barrier attributed to bulk HEAs.
Chemical short-range order and ordered clusters can develop in an equiatomic five-component refractory HEA.
Nanoparticle structural evolution will be dominated by surface-induced ordering and phase separation rather than random-solid-solution stability.
Surface segregation and ordering will cause HENA nanoparticles to become ordered or multiphase at substantially lower temperatures than bulk HEAs.
Diffusion in traditional bulk alloys is bulk-limited, whereas surface diffusion dominates in HENA nanoparticles.
The nanoparticles initially have a disordered, nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal solid-solution structure.
Heating between 500 and 1000 degrees Celsius for minutes to hours will induce thermal evolution and atomic diffusion in particles smaller than 50 nm.
Surface energy promotes elemental segregation and ordering in these nanoparticles.
Surface diffusion provides a fast pathway that bypasses sluggish bulk diffusion and permits phase separation or ordering.
Short-range order or ordered clusters are thermodynamically favored at lower temperatures in nanoparticles than in bulk alloys.
The surface contribution to Gibbs free energy can drive segregation of particular elements to reduce surface tension.
Heated HENA nanoparticles will rapidly form ordered clusters or undergo phase separation.
The nanoparticle diffusion coefficient will be orders of magnitude greater than that of bulk material with the same composition.
Surface segregation may produce a core-shell structure or a disordered core with an ordered shell.
Bulk Al_xCoCrFeNi and NbTaTiV alloys generally maintain single-phase stability and sluggish diffusion to high temperatures because of configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
Surface effects become negligible when the nanoparticles exceed 100 nm in size.
Exceptionally low surface energy would prevent surface-energy-driven segregation and invalidate the proposed mechanism.
A synthesis route that produces a thermodynamically stable ordered nanoparticle structure would invalidate the assumed disordered initial state and associated instability pathway.
